transcript: alright there's gonna be some controversial discourse about this upcoming Broadway show so why don't we just get a head start on it? it was just announced that “Gloria” by acclaimed playwright Branden Jacobs-Jenkins is coming to Broadway this is a play that premiered in 2015 at the Vineyard Theatre off-Broadway and it was generally very well-received it was a finalist for the Pulitzer I saw a production of it at my college and I thought it was excellent but the play presents a thorny problem for any theatre putting it on and the audiences going to see it which is that it has one scene in particular that some viewers might find very upsetting but it's the most important scene in the play and it's a huge spoiler. I'm sure second Stage, the theatre company putting it on will make content warnings available to anyone who seeks them out. but the question is: if you're an audience member how do you assess whether this play may or may not be for you without spoiling it? you might actually find that you think you totally can handle it but by then it's too late. I guess ultimately, the answer to that part is fairly straightforward like if you, specifically, are concerned that this might be an issue it is ultimately better to spoil it than risk having like a really bad time at the theatre because, you know…priorities. but if you think you can handle some shock I would recommend going into this knowing as little as possible. even still I'm sure some people are gonna say that it's irresponsible to even put a play like this on stage especially because there will inevitably be people who go in blind and leave pretty upset. so I really don't envy anyone who has to work front of house for any production of this play but let alone one with the increased visibility and expectations of Broadway. it might be a rough time, but I do think this play is very good and deserves to be revived just maybe approach with caution
